title.zh: 卷265 列傳五十二 汤斌 陆陇其 张伯行
title.en: Volume 265 Biographies 52: Tang Bin, Lu Longqi, Zhang Boxing
title.raw: 卷265 列傳五十二 汤斌 陆陇其 张伯行

sentences.zh: 列傳五十二

translations.literal: Biographies 52
translations.idiomatic: Biography 52

sentences.zh: 湯斌孫之旭陸隴其張伯行

translations.literal: Tang Bin, Sun Zhixu, Lu Longqi, Zhang Boxing
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, Sun Zhixu, Lu Longqi, and Zhang Boxing

sentences.zh: 湯斌，字孔伯，河南睢州人。

translations.literal: Tang Bin, style name Kongbo, was a native of Suizhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, whose style was Kongbo, came from Suizhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 明末流賊陷睢州，母趙殉節死，事具明史列女傳。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, roving bandits captured Suizhou; his mother Zhao died a martyr's death, the affair being recorded in the Ming History biographies of exemplary women.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel armies overran Suizhou in the late Ming, his mother Zhao chose death rather than dishonor; her story is told in the Ming History's biographies of virtuous women.

sentences.zh: 父契祖，挈斌避兵浙江衢州。

translations.literal: His father Qizu took Bin and fled the warfare to Quzhou in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qizu took him to Quzhou in Zhejiang to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，奉父還裡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he brought his father back home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1645 he brought his father home.

sentences.zh: 九年，成進士，選庶吉士，授國史院檢討。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1652 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer, and was made a reviser at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 方議修明史，斌應詔言：「宋史修於元至正，而不諱文天祥、謝枋得之忠；

translations.literal: When the Ming History was under discussion for compilation, Bin responded to an imperial edict, saying: "The Song History was compiled in the Zhizheng era of Yuan, yet it did not conceal the loyalty of Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde;
translations.idiomatic: While plans were being made to compile the Ming History, Bin answered an imperial summons with a memorial: "The Song History was written under the Yuan, yet it still honored Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde for their loyalty;

sentences.zh: 元史修於明洪武，而亦著丁好禮、巴顏布哈之義。

translations.literal: the Yuan History was compiled in the Hongwu reign of Ming, yet it also records the righteousness of Ding Haoli and Bayan Buha.
translations.idiomatic: the Yuan History was compiled in early Ming, yet it likewise records the integrity of Ding Haoli and Bayan Buha.

sentences.zh: 順治元、二年間，前明諸臣有抗節不屈、臨危致命者，不可概以叛書。

translations.literal: In the first and second years of Shunzhi, among former Ming officials there were those who resisted to the end and died facing peril; they cannot all be written down as rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In 1644 and 1645 many former Ming officials held firm and died rather than submit; they must not all be branded as traitors in the record.

sentences.zh: 宜命纂修諸臣勿事瞻顧。

translations.literal: The compiling officials should be ordered not to look over their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers should be instructed to write without fear or favor.

sentences.zh: 」下所司。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent to the relevant departments.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮銓、金之俊謂斌獎逆，擬旨嚴飭，世祖特召至南苑慰諭之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Feng Quan and Jin Zhijun said Bin was praising rebellion and drafted an edict of severe reprimand; the Shizu Emperor specially summoned him to the Southern Park to console and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Feng Quan and Jin Zhijun accused him of glorifying rebellion and drafted a stern reprimand, but the Shunzhi Emperor summoned him to the Southern Park and reassured him in person.

sentences.zh: 時府、道多缺員，上以用人方亟，當得文行兼優者，以學問為經濟，選翰林官，得陳爌、黃志遴、王無咎、楊思聖、藍潤、王舜年、範週、馬燁曾、沈荃及斌凡十人。

translations.literal: At the time many prefectural and circuit posts were vacant; the emperor, urgently needing men, sought those combining literary and moral excellence, taking learning as practical statecraft, and selected Hanlin officials, obtaining Chen Huang, Huang Zhilin, Wang Wujiu, Yang Sisheng, Lan Run, Wang Shunnian, Fan Zhou, Ma Yeeng, Shen Quan, and Bin, ten in all.
translations.idiomatic: Many prefectural and circuit posts stood empty, and the emperor wanted men of both learning and integrity who could turn scholarship to practical use. From the Hanlin Academy he chose Chen Huang, Huang Zhilin, Wang Wujiu, Yang Sisheng, Lan Run, Wang Shunnian, Fan Zhou, Ma Yeeng, Shen Quan, and Bin—ten in all.

sentences.zh: 斌出為潼關道副使。

translations.literal: Bin went out as vice commissioner of the Tongguan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was posted as vice commissioner of the Tongguan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵關中，徵發四至。

translations.literal: At the time military operations were underway in Guanzhong, and levies arrived from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was fighting in the Guanzhong region, and requisitions poured in from every direction.

sentences.zh: 總兵陳德調湖南，將二萬人至關欲留，斌以計出之，至洛陽譁潰。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Chen De was transferred to Hunan; leading twenty thousand men to the pass he wished to remain, but Bin by stratagem got them out; at Luoyang they mutinied and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Chen De was reassigned to Hunan but brought twenty thousand troops to Tong Pass intending to stay. Bin contrived to send them on; at Luoyang they rioted and broke apart.

sentences.zh: 十六年，調江西嶺北道。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was transferred to the Lingbei Circuit of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1659 he was transferred to the Lingbei Circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明將李玉廷率所部萬人據雩都山寨，約降，未及期，而鄭成功犯江寧。

translations.literal: Ming general Li Yuting led ten thousand of his troops to hold a mountain stockade at Yudu, having agreed to surrender; before the appointed date, Zheng Chenggong attacked Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming loyalist Li Yuting held a mountain stronghold at Yudu with ten thousand men and had agreed to surrender, but before the deadline Zheng Chenggong struck at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 斌策玉廷必變計，夜馳至南安設守。

translations.literal: Bin calculated that Yuting would change his plan, and rode through the night to Nan'an to set up defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Bin judged that Yuting would renege, rode overnight to Nan'an, and organized its defense.

sentences.zh: 玉廷以兵至，見有備，卻走；

translations.literal: Yuting came with troops, saw preparations in place, and withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: Yuting marched up, found the defenses ready, and retreated;

sentences.zh: 遣將追擊，獲玉廷。

translations.literal: he sent generals in pursuit and captured Yuting.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent troops after him and took Yuting prisoner.

sentences.zh: 斌念父老，以病乞休，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Bin, mindful of his aged father, pleaded illness to retire, and entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of his elderly father, Bin asked to retire on grounds of illness and then mourned his father's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，聞容城孫奇逢講學夏峰，負笈往從。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, hearing that Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng was lecturing at Xiafeng, he shouldered his books and went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he heard that Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng was teaching at Xiafeng and went to join him as a student.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，詔舉博學鴻儒，尚書魏象樞、副都御史金鋐以斌薦，試一等，授翰林院侍講，與修明史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, an edict summoned erudite scholars; Minister Wei Xiangshu and Vice Censor-in-Chief Jin E recommended Bin; he placed first in the examination, was appointed Hanlin lecturer, and took part in compiling the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: In 1678 the court called for eminent scholars; Wei Xiangshu and Jin E recommended Bin, who ranked first in the special examination and became a Hanlin lecturer working on the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 二十年，充日講起居注官、浙江鄉試正考官，轉侍讀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he served as daily lecturer and recorder of the emperor's movements, chief examiner of the Zhejiang provincial examination, and was transferred to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In 1681 he became a daily lecturer and diarist of the imperial court, served as chief examiner for the Zhejiang provincial exams, and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命為明史總裁官，遷左庶子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, he was appointed chief compiler of the Ming History and promoted to left vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1682 he was named chief compiler of the Ming History and made left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 1684 he was elevated to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 江寧巡撫缺，方廷推，上曰：「今以道學名者，言行或相悖。

translations.literal: The Jiangning governorship was vacant and the court was deliberating candidates; the emperor said: "Those famed today for Neo-Confucian learning often contradict their words with their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangning governorship fell vacant and the court was nominating candidates, the emperor remarked, "Men who parade as Neo-Confucian sages often fail to live up to their reputations.

sentences.zh: 朕聞​​湯斌從孫奇逢學，有操守，可補江寧巡撫。

translations.literal: I have heard that Tang Bin studied under Sun Qifeng and has integrity; he may fill the Jiangning governorship."
translations.idiomatic: I am told Tang Bin studied with Sun Qifeng and has real integrity. He should take Jiangning."

sentences.zh: 」瀕行，諭曰：「居官以正風俗為先。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he was instructed: "In office, correcting customs comes first.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, the emperor told him, "Your first duty in office is to set society's morals right.

sentences.zh: 江蘇習尚華侈，其加意化導，非旦夕事，必從容漸摩，使之改心易慮。

translations.literal: Jiangsu's habits tend toward luxury; to devote care to transforming and guiding them is no overnight matter—you must gradually influence them with patience until they change their hearts and alter their thinking."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu is steeped in extravagance. Reforming it will take time; work patiently and let people change their ways by degrees."

sentences.zh: 」賜鞍馬一、表裡十、銀五百。

translations.literal: He was granted one saddle horse, ten sets of outer and inner garments, and five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a saddle horse, ten sets of robes, and five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 复賜御書三軸，曰：「今當遠離，展此如對朕也！

translations.literal: He was again granted three scrolls of imperial calligraphy, reading: "You are now going far away—when you unroll these it will be as if facing me!"
translations.idiomatic: He also received three scrolls of the emperor's own writing with the message, "You are going far from court; open these as though you were standing before me!"

sentences.zh: 」十月，上南巡，至蘇州，諭斌曰：「向聞吳閶繁盛，今觀其風土，尚虛華，安佚樂，逐末者多，力田者寡。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the emperor made a southern tour; reaching Suzhou, he told Bin: "I had heard that Wu's Chang Gate district was flourishing; now observing its customs, they are still given to empty display, ease, and pleasure—many chase secondary trades, few labor in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on his southern tour, the emperor reached Suzhou and said to Bin, "I had heard that the district around Chang Gate was thriving, but what I see is still vanity, idleness, and pleasure-seeking. Too many chase trade; too few till the soil.

sentences.zh: 爾當使之去奢返樸，事事務本，庶幾可挽頹風。

translations.literal: You must make them abandon luxury and return to simplicity, in every matter attend to fundamentals—then perhaps the declining trend can be reversed."
translations.idiomatic: You must lead them back from extravagance to simplicity and make every affair turn on essentials. Only then may this decaying custom be turned around."

sentences.zh: 」上還蹕，斌從至江寧，命還蘇州，賜御書及狐腋蟒服。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Bin accompanied him to Jiangning; he was ordered back to Suzhou and granted imperial calligraphy and a python robe lined with fox fur.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey Bin accompanied him as far as Jiangning, then was sent back to Suzhou with imperial calligraphy and a python robe lined with fox fur.

sentences.zh: 初，餘國柱為江寧巡撫，淮、揚二府被水，國柱疏言：「水退，田可耕，明年當徵賦。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu Guozhu was Jiangning governor, Huai and Yang prefectures suffered flooding; Guozhu memorialized: "When the water recedes the fields can be cultivated; next year taxes should be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yu Guozhu governed Jiangning, floods struck Huai and Yang prefectures. Guozhu reported that once the waters fell the fields could be planted and taxes should be levied the following year.

sentences.zh: 」斌遣覆勘，水未退即田，出水處猶未可耕，奏寢前議。

translations.literal: " Bin sent men to reinvestigate; where water had not yet receded they were already counted as fields, and drained areas were still uncultivable; he memorialized to shelve the earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Bin ordered a fresh survey and found fields still underwater and drained land not yet fit to plant. He memorialized to set aside Guozhu's plan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，疏言：「江蘇賦稅甲天下，每歲本折五六百萬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he memorialized: "Jiangsu's taxes rank first in the empire, amounting to five or six million taels in grain and silver each year.
translations.idiomatic: In 1685 he wrote, "Jiangsu's tax burden leads the empire, with annual payments in grain and silver reaching five or six million taels.

sentences.zh: 上命分年帶徵漕欠，而地丁錢糧，自康熙十八年至二十二年，五年並徵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered arrears in grain transport tax to be collected over successive years, but land and poll taxes from the eighteenth through the twenty-second year of Kangxi were levied in a single five-year collection.
translations.idiomatic: The court had allowed transport-tax arrears to be collected year by year, but land and poll taxes from 1679 through 1683 were being demanded all at once.

sentences.zh: 州縣比較，十日一限。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties held comparative assessments with a deadline every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Counties faced collection deadlines every ten days.

sentences.zh: 使每日輪比，則十日中三日空閒，七日赴比。

translations.literal: If daily rotation were used for comparison, then in ten days three would be idle and seven spent at assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Even with daily rotation, peasants had only three days in ten free of the tax office; seven were consumed by collection.

sentences.zh: 民知剜補無術，拌皮骨以捱徵比；

translations.literal: The people knew there was no way to make good the shortfall and stripped flesh from bone to endure the levies;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they could never make up what they owed, commoners stripped themselves to the bone to meet each deadline;

sentences.zh: 官知催科計窮，拌降革以圖卸擔。

translations.literal: officials knew their collection schemes were exhausted and risked demotion or dismissal to shed the burden.
translations.idiomatic: while officials, seeing collection tactics fail, accepted demotion or dismissal rather than keep squeezing the people.

sentences.zh: 懇將民欠地丁錢糧照漕項一例，於康熙二十四年起，分年帶徵。

translations.literal: He begged that popular arrears in land and poll taxes, following the precedent of transport tax, from the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi onward be collected over successive years.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that peasant arrears in land and poll tax be collected over several years, as with transport tax, beginning in 1685.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「蘇、鬆土隘人稠，而條銀漕白正耗以及白糧經費漕賸五米十銀，雜項差徭，不可勝計。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Suzhou and Songjiang have narrow land and dense population, yet itemized silver, transport surcharges, standard and extra grain levies, white-grain expenses, transport surplus, five-grain and ten-silver charges, and miscellaneous corvée cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that Suzhou and Songjiang were crowded on little land yet bore itemized silver dues, transport surcharges, standard and supplemental grain levies, white-grain fees, transport reserves, and countless miscellaneous corvées.

sentences.zh: 區區兩府，田不加廣，而當大省百餘州縣之賦，民力日絀。

translations.literal: These two small prefectures, their fields not expanding, yet bear the tax load of more than a hundred prefectures and counties of a great province—the people's strength daily fails.
translations.idiomatic: Two prefectures alone, without more farmland, carried a burden equal to that of a hundred counties elsewhere, and the people's strength was failing day by day.

sentences.zh: 順治初，錢糧起存相半，考成之例尚寬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, grain and silver remitted and retained were about equal, and the performance-assessment rules were still lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign only half of collected taxes had to be forwarded immediately, and performance reviews were still lenient.

sentences.zh: 後因兵餉急迫，起解數多，又定十分考成之例。

translations.literal: Later, because military funds were urgent, the amounts forwarded increased, and the rule of full ten-tenths assessment was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, military needs forced larger remittances and a rule requiring one hundred percent collection.

sentences.zh: 一分不完，難逭部議。

translations.literal: One tenth uncompleted could not escape censure from the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: A single tenth short invited censure from the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 官吏顧惜功名，必多苟且。

translations.literal: Officials, cherishing their reputations, necessarily resorted to much expediency.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, anxious to protect their careers, resorted to every expedient.

sentences.zh: 參罰期迫，則以欠作完；

translations.literal: When the deadline for punishment drew near, they reported arrears as complete;
translations.idiomatic: As punishment deadlines neared, they reported shortfalls as paid;

sentences.zh: 賠補維艱，又以完為欠。

translations.literal: when making good payments was difficult, they turned completed amounts into arrears.
translations.idiomatic: when reimbursement proved impossible, they turned completed payments back into arrears.

sentences.zh: 百姓脂膏已竭，有司智勇俱困。

translations.literal: The people's fat and marrow were exhausted; local officials were trapped in wit and courage alike.
translations.idiomatic: The people had been bled dry, and local officials were at their wits' end.

sentences.zh: 積欠年久，惟恃恩蠲。

translations.literal: Arrears accumulated over years could only await imperial grace for remission.
translations.idiomatic: Years of arrears could be cleared only by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 然與其赦免於追呼既窮之後，何若酌減於徵比未加之先。

translations.literal: Yet rather than pardoning after pursuit and summons had reached their limit, how much better to reduce judiciously before levies were imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Better to reduce the burden before collection drives people to ruin than to remit taxes after they have already been crushed.

sentences.zh: 懇將蘇、松錢糧各照科則量減一二成，定適中可完之實數，再將科則稍加歸併，使簡易明白，便於稽覈。

translations.literal: He begged that Suzhou and Songjiang grain and silver taxes each be reduced by one or two tenths according to the tax schedule, fixing a moderate actual amount that could be completed, then slightly consolidating the schedule to make it simple and clear for audit.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Suzhou and Songjiang taxes be cut by ten or twenty percent according to the statutory rates, that a realistic payable figure be set, and that the schedules be simplified for easier auditing.

sentences.zh: 」又請蠲蘇、松等七府州十三年至十七年未完銀米，淮、揚二府十八九兩年災欠，及邳州版荒、宿遷九釐地畝款項，並失額丁糧，皆下部議行。

translations.literal: " He also requested remission of unpaid silver and grain in seven prefectures and departments including Suzhou and Songjiang from the thirteenth through seventeenth years, disaster arrears in Huai and Yang in the eighteenth and nineteenth years, Pi prefecture's wasteland and Suqian's nine-fen land assessments, and lost quota poll taxes—all referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " He also sought remission of unpaid taxes from 1674 through 1678 in seven prefectures including Suzhou and Songjiang, disaster arrears in Huai and Yang from 1679 and 1680, wasteland assessments in Pi and the nine-fen land tax in Suqian, and lost poll-tax quotas. All were sent to the ministries and approved.

sentences.zh: 九釐地畝款項，即明萬曆後暫加三餉，宿遷派銀四千三百有奇，至是始得蠲免。

translations.literal: The nine-fen land assessment was the temporary Three Levies added after the Wanli reign of Ming; Suqian was assessed more than four thousand three hundred taels of silver, and only now obtained remission.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-fen land tax was a surcharge dating from the Ming Wanli era's Three Levies; Suqian alone owed more than 4,300 taels, remitted only now.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚、徐三府復水，斌條列蠲賑事宜，請發帑五萬，糴米湖廣，下俟詔下，即行諮請漕運總督徐旭齡、河道總督靳輔分賑淮安。

translations.literal: Huai, Yang, and Xu prefectures flooded again; Bin itemized matters for remission and relief, requesting fifty thousand taels from the treasury and purchase of grain in Huguang; once the edict was issued he would immediately consult Grain Transport Director Xu Xuling and River Conservancy Director Jin Fu to distribute relief at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai, Yang, and Xu flooded again, Bin laid out a relief plan: fifty thousand taels from the treasury and grain bought in Huguang, with Grain Transport Director Xu Xuling and River Director Jin Fu to distribute aid at Huai'an once the edict arrived.

sentences.zh: 斌赴清河、桃源、宿遷、邳、豐諸州縣察賑，疏聞，上命侍郎素赫助之。

translations.literal: Bin went to Qinghe, Taoyuan, Suqian, Pi, and Feng counties to inspect relief; memorializing the facts, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Suhe to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Bin inspected relief work in Qinghe, Taoyuan, Suqian, Pi, and Feng and reported back; the emperor sent Vice Minister Suhe to help.

sentences.zh: 先後奏劾知府趙祿星、張萬壽，知縣陳協濬、蔡司霑、盧綖、葛之英、劉濤、劉茂位等。

translations.literal: He successively memorialized impeaching prefects Zhao Luxing and Zhang Wanshou, and magistrates Chen Xiejun, Cai Sizhan, Lu Yan, Ge Zhiying, Liu Tao, Liu Maowei, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached in turn the prefects Zhao Luxing and Zhang Wanshou and the magistrates Chen Xiejun, Cai Sizhan, Lu Yan, Ge Zhiying, Liu Tao, Liu Maowei, and others.

sentences.zh: 常州知府祖進朝以失察屬吏降調，斌察其廉，奏留之。

translations.literal: Changzhou Prefect Zu Jinchao was demoted for failure to supervise subordinates; Bin found him incorrupt and memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou Prefect Zu Jinchao was demoted for lax supervision of his staff, but Bin found him honest and asked that he be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 又疏薦吳縣知縣劉滋、吳江知縣郭琇廉能最著，而徵收錢糧，未能十分全完，請予行取。

translations.literal: He also memorialized recommending Wu County Magistrate Liu Zi and Wujiang Magistrate Guo Xiu as most outstanding in integrity and ability, yet in collecting grain and silver they could not achieve full completion; he asked that they be selected for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Liu Zi of Wu County and Guo Xiu of Wujiang as the most upright and capable magistrates, though they had not collected taxes in full, and asked that they be promoted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 下部皆議駁，特旨允行。

translations.literal: The ministries all deliberated and rejected; a special edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries rejected both requests, but the emperor overruled them by special edict.

sentences.zh: 斌令諸州縣立社學，講孝經、小學，修泰伯祠及宋范仲淹、明周順昌祠，禁婦女遊觀，胥吏、倡優毋得衣裘帛，毀淫詞小說，革火葬。

translations.literal: Bin ordered all prefectures and counties to establish community schools, lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning, restored the shrine of Taibo and the Song's Fan Zhongyan and Ming's Zhou Shunchang, forbade women from sightseeing excursions, clerks and actors from wearing fur and silk, destroyed licentious ballads and novels, and abolished cremation.
translations.idiomatic: Bin ordered community schools in every county to teach the Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning, restored shrines to Taibo, Fan Zhongyan, and Zhou Shunchang, barred women from pleasure outings and clerks and actors from wearing silk and fur, burned obscene books, and ended cremation.

sentences.zh: 蘇州城西上方山有五通神祠，幾數百年，遠近奔走如騖。

translations.literal: West of Suzhou city on Shangfang Mountain stood a shrine to the Five-Passage Spirit, for nearly several hundred years with people from far and near rushing like a stampede.
translations.idiomatic: West of Suzhou, on Mount Shangfang, stood a shrine to the Five-Passage Spirit that for centuries drew crowds from far and wide.

sentences.zh: 諺謂其山曰「肉山」，其下石湖曰「酒海」。

translations.literal: A proverb called the mountain "Flesh Mountain" and the Stone Lake below "Sea of Wine."
translations.idiomatic: Locals called the mountain "Flesh Mountain" and the Stone Lake below it "Sea of Wine."

sentences.zh: 少婦病，巫輒言五通將娶為婦，往往瘵死。

translations.literal: When young women fell ill, shamans would say the Five-Passage Spirit would take them as wives, and they often died of consumption.
translations.idiomatic: When young women fell ill, shamans declared that the spirit would marry them, and many wasted away and died.

sentences.zh: 斌收其偶像，木者焚之，土者沉之，並飭諸州縣有類此者悉毀之，撤其材修學宮。

translations.literal: Bin seized its idols—wooden ones he burned, earthen ones he sank—and ordered all prefectures and counties to destroy similar shrines, using their timber to repair the school temples.
translations.idiomatic: Bin seized the idols, burned those of wood and sank those of clay, ordered every county to destroy similar shrines, and used the timber to repair school temples.

sentences.zh: 教化大行，民皆悅服。

translations.literal: Moral transformation was widely carried out, and the people all submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: His moral reforms took hold, and the people accepted them willingly.

sentences.zh: 方明珠用事，國柱附之。

translations.literal: At the time Songgotu held power, and Guozhu attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was in power, and Yu Guozhu attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 布政使龔其旋坐貪，為御史陸隴其所劾，因國柱賄明珠得緩；

translations.literal: Provincial Treasurer Gong Qixuan was convicted of corruption and impeached by Censor Lu Longqi; through Guozhu's bribe to Songgotu the case was eased;
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Treasurer Gong Qixuan was impeached for corruption by Censor Lu Longqi, but Guozhu bribed Songgotu and the case was softened;

sentences.zh: 國柱更欲為斌言，以斌嚴正，不得發。

translations.literal: Guozhu further wished to speak on Bin's behalf, but because Bin was stern and upright he could not bring it up.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu wanted to speak for Bin as well, but Bin's rectitude left him no opening.

sentences.zh: 及蠲江南賦，國柱使人語斌，謂皆明珠力，江南人宜有以報之，索賕，斌不應。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan taxes were remitted, Guozhu sent someone to tell Bin that it was all Songgotu's doing and Jiangnan people ought to repay him, demanding a bribe; Bin did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiangnan tax remissions, Guozhu sent word that Songgotu deserved gratitude from the region and demanded a payoff. Bin refused.

sentences.zh: 比大計，外吏輦金於明珠門者不絕，而斌屬吏獨無。

translations.literal: At the grand assessment, outer officials bearing gold to Songgotu's gate never ceased, but among Bin's subordinates there was none.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation, officials streamed gold to Songgotu's door, but none of Bin's staff did.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上為太子擇輔導臣，廷臣有舉斌者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the emperor was selecting tutors for the crown prince; court officials recommended Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1686 the emperor sought tutors for the crown prince, and officials recommended Bin.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自古帝王諭教太子，必簡和平謹恪之臣，統率宮僚，專資輔翼。

translations.literal: An edict said: "From antiquity emperors instructing the crown prince have always selected peaceful, careful, and respectful ministers to lead the palace staff and devote themselves to assistance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Since antiquity, emperors teaching their heirs have chosen calm, careful men to lead the palace staff and guide the prince.

sentences.zh: 湯斌在講筵時，素行謹慎，朕所稔知。

translations.literal: Tang Bin at the lecture hall has always been careful in conduct, as I am well acquainted.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin has long been careful in conduct at the lecture hall, as I know well.

sentences.zh: 及簡任巡撫，潔己率屬，實心任事。

translations.literal: When appointed governor, he purified himself and led his subordinates, serving affairs with a sincere heart.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he kept himself pure, set an example for his staff, and served with wholehearted devotion.

sentences.zh: 允宜拔擢，以風有位。

translations.literal: He is truly fit for promotion, to set an example for those in office."
translations.idiomatic: He should be promoted to set an example for all in office."

sentences.zh: 」授禮部尚書，管詹事府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites and superintendent of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 將行，吳民泣留不得，罷市三日，遮道焚香送之。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Wu people wept and begged him to stay but could not; markets closed for three days, and they blocked the road burning incense to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, the people of Wu wept and tried to detain him, closed their markets for three days, and lined the road burning incense to see him off.

sentences.zh: 初，靳輔與按察使於成龍爭論下河事，久未決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong disputed the lower-river project, long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong had disputed whether to dredge the lower Yellow River, and the matter had dragged on.

sentences.zh: 廷臣阿明珠意，多右輔。

translations.literal: Court officials curried Songgotu's favor and mostly sided with Jin Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Most courtiers sided with Jin Fu to please Songgotu.

sentences.zh: 命尚書薩穆哈、穆成額會斌勘議，斌主濬下河如成龍言。

translations.literal: Ministers Samuha and Mucheng'e were ordered to join Bin in investigation and deliberation; Bin advocated dredging the lower river as Chenglong had said.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Samuha and Mucheng'e were sent with Bin to inspect the works; Bin sided with Chenglong's plan to dredge the lower river.

sentences.zh: 薩穆哈等還京師，不以斌語聞。

translations.literal: Samuha and the others returned to the capital without reporting Bin's words.
translations.idiomatic: Samuha and the others returned to the capital without reporting Bin's opinion.

sentences.zh: 斌至，上問斌，斌以實對。

translations.literal: When Bin arrived, the emperor questioned Bin, and Bin answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin arrived, the emperor questioned him, and he answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 薩穆哈等坐罷去。

translations.literal: Samuha and the others were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Samuha and his colleagues were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十六年五月，不雨，靈臺郎董漢臣上書指斥時事，語侵執政，下廷議，明珠惶懼，將引罪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year there was no rain; Astronomy Bureau Attendant Dong Hanchen submitted a memorial criticizing current affairs, his words encroaching on those in power; it was referred to court deliberation; Songgotu was fearful and about to plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 1687, amid drought, Astronomy Bureau clerk Dong Hanchen memorialized criticizing current affairs in terms that implicated the chief ministers. The case went to court debate; Songgotu was terrified and prepared to confess guilt.

sentences.zh: 大學士王熙獨曰：「市兒妄語，立斬之，事畢矣。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Xi alone said: "Street boys' reckless talk—execute him at once and the matter is finished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Xi alone said, "It is the babble of a market loafer. Behead him at once and the affair is closed.

sentences.zh: 」斌後至，國柱以告。

translations.literal: " Bin arrived later; Guozhu told him.
translations.idiomatic: " Bin arrived afterward, and Guozhu told him what Wang Xi had said.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「漢臣應詔言事無死法。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Hanchen responded to an edict to speak on affairs—there is no capital statute for this.
translations.idiomatic: Bin replied, "Hanchen answered an imperial summons to speak. There is no law that calls for his death.

sentences.zh: 大臣不言而小臣言之，吾輩當自省。

translations.literal: When great ministers do not speak and minor officials do, we ought to examine ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers are silent and junior officials speak up, we ought to look to ourselves."

sentences.zh: 」上卒免漢臣罪。

translations.literal: The emperor finally pardoned Hanchen's offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally spared Hanchen.

sentences.zh: 明珠、國柱愈恚，摘其語上聞，並摭斌在蘇時文告語，曰「愛民有心，救民無術」，以為謗訕，傳旨詰問。

translations.literal: Songgotu and Guozhu grew more resentful, excerpted his words to report upward, and also gathered phrases from Bin's proclamations in Suzhou saying "he has a heart to love the people but no method to save them," treating them as slander; an edict was transmitted to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu and Guozhu were enraged, reported Bin's words to the throne, and dredged up a phrase from his Suzhou proclamations—"he loves the people in heart but lacks the means to save them"—as slander. An edict ordered him questioned.

sentences.zh: 斌惟自陳資性愚昧，愆過叢集，乞賜嚴加處分。

translations.literal: Bin only confessed that his nature was foolish, his faults numerous, and begged severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bin could only confess his own dullness and many faults and ask for stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 左都御史璙丹、王鴻緒等又連疏劾斌。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Langdan, Wang Hongxu, and others again submitted successive memorials impeaching Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Langdan, Wang Hongxu, and others followed with memorial after memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 會斌先薦候補道耿介為少詹事，同輔太子，介以老疾乞休。

translations.literal: It happened that Bin had earlier recommended the expectant official Geng Jie as junior mentor, jointly assisting the crown prince; Jie pleaded old age and illness to retire.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Bin had earlier recommended the expectant official Geng Jie as junior mentor to assist the crown prince; Jie now asked to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 詹事尹泰等劾介僥倖求去，且及斌妄薦，議奪斌官，上獨留斌任。

translations.literal: Household Tutor Yin Tai and others impeached Jie for seeking leave by presumptuous luck, and also charged Bin with reckless recommendation; deliberation proposed stripping Bin of office, but the emperor alone retained Bin in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Household Tutor Yin Tai and others accused Geng Jie of using illness as a pretext to quit and charged Bin with a reckless appointment. The court proposed stripping Bin of office, but the emperor kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 國柱宣言上將隸斌旗籍，斌適扶病入朝，道路相傳，聞者皆泣下。

translations.literal: Guozhu declared that the emperor would enroll Bin in the banner registers; Bin happened to attend court supporting himself in illness, and along the roads the rumor spread—those who heard all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu spread word that the emperor would reduce Bin to banner status. Bin came to court leaning on attendants, ill; the rumor spread through the streets and those who heard it wept.

sentences.zh: 江南人客都下者，將擊登聞鼓訟冤，繼知無其事，乃散。

translations.literal: Jiangnan people lodging in the capital were about to strike the petition drum to sue for injustice; learning there was no such matter, they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan natives in the capital nearly struck the petition drum to protest on his behalf, but learning the rumor false, they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 九月，改工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，疾作，遣太醫診視。

translations.literal: Before long illness set in, and imperial physicians were sent to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill, and court physicians were sent to treat him.

sentences.zh: 十月，自通州勘貢木歸，一夕卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, returning from Tongzhou after inspecting tribute timber, he died in a single night, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, returning from Tongzhou after inspecting tribute timber, he died overnight at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 斌既卒，上嘗語廷臣曰：「朕遇湯斌不薄，而怨訕不休，何也？

translations.literal: After Bin died, the emperor once told court officials: "I treated Tang Bin not ungenerously, yet resentment and slander never ceased—why?
translations.idiomatic: After Bin's death the emperor once asked his ministers, "I treated Tang Bin well enough. Why did the grumbling never stop?

sentences.zh: 」明珠、國柱輩嫉斌甚，微上厚斌，斌禍且不測。

translations.literal: " Songgotu, Guozhu, and their faction envied Bin deeply; had the emperor not favored Bin slightly, Bin's disaster would have been beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: " Songgotu, Guozhu, and their allies hated him fiercely. Had the emperor not favored him a little, Bin's ruin would have been certain.

sentences.zh: 斌既師奇逢，習宋諸儒書。

translations.literal: Bin had studied under Sun Qifeng and was versed in the books of the Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Bin studied under Sun Qifeng and mastered the Song Neo-Confucian classics.

sentences.zh: 嘗訂：「滯事物以窮理，沉溺跡象，既支離而無本；

translations.literal: He once formulated: "Clinging to things to exhaust principle, drowning in traces and appearances, is already fragmented and rootless;
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote, "To cling to things in order to grasp principle, drowning in appearances, is to end up fragmented and rootless;

sentences.zh: 離事物而致知，隳聰黜明，亦虛空而鮮實。

translations.literal: to leave things and seek knowledge, destroying intelligence and banishing clarity, is likewise empty and rarely substantial."
translations.idiomatic: to leave things behind and seek knowledge apart from them, dulling the mind, is likewise empty and rarely real."

sentences.zh: 」其教人，以為必先明義利之界，謹誠偽之關，為真經學、真道學；

translations.literal: In teaching others he held that one must first clarify the boundary between righteousness and profit and carefully guard the gate between sincerity and pretense, thereby becoming true classical learning and true moral learning;
translations.idiomatic: In teaching he insisted that one must first distinguish righteousness from profit and sincerity from pretense—only then could one practice true classical learning and true moral philosophy;

sentences.zh: 否則講論、踐履析為二事，世道何賴。

translations.literal: otherwise discourse and practice are split into two affairs—on what can the age rely?
translations.idiomatic: otherwise talk and action split apart, and what can the world depend on?

sentences.zh: 斌篤守程、硃，亦不薄王守仁。

translations.literal: Bin devotedly upheld Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, yet did not slight Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Bin held firmly to Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, yet did not dismiss Wang Yangming.

sentences.zh: 身體力行，不尚講論，所詣深粹。

translations.literal: He embodied practice in person, did not esteem mere discourse, and what he attained was deep and pure.
translations.idiomatic: He lived what he taught rather than prize debate alone, and his attainment was deep and refined.

sentences.zh: 著有洛學編、潛庵語錄。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Luoyang Learning and the Recorded Sayings of the Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Records of Luoyang Learning and Recorded Sayings of the Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，入賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was entered in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng era he was enshrined in the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，諡文正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was posthumously titled Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was given the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，從祀孔子廟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he was granted attendant sacrifice in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he was admitted to attendant sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 孫之旭，字孟升。

translations.literal: Sun Zhixu, style name Mengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhixu, whose style was Mengsheng,

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士，官編修，改御史。

translations.literal: became a jinshi in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi, served as compiler, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: passed the jinshi examination in 1706, served as a Hanlin compiler, and became a censor.

sentences.zh: 出為霸昌道，內遷左通政。

translations.literal: He went out as Baxing Circuit commissioner and was promoted within the capital to left vice commissioner of communications.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Baxing Circuit and later promoted to left vice commissioner of communications in the capital.

sentences.zh: 所至皆有聲。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he won a reputation.

sentences.zh: 陸隴其，初名龍其，字稼書，浙江平湖人。

translations.literal: Lu Longqi, original name Longqi, style name Jiashu, was a native of Pinghu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Longqi, originally named Longqi and styled Jiashu, came from Pinghu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1670.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授江南嘉定知縣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Jiading in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1675 he was appointed magistrate of Jiading in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定大縣，賦多俗侈。

translations.literal: Jiading was a large county with heavy taxes and extravagant customs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading was a large county with heavy taxes and extravagant habits.

sentences.zh: 隴其守約持儉，務以德化民。

translations.literal: Longqi kept to simplicity and thrift, striving to transform the people through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Longqi lived simply and thriftily and sought to reform the people through moral example.

sentences.zh: 或父訟子，泣而諭之，子掖父歸而善事焉；

translations.literal: When a father sued his son, he wept and admonished them; the son supported his father home and thereafter served him well;
translations.idiomatic: When a father sued his son, he wept and reasoned with them until the son led his father home and treated him well;

sentences.zh: 弟訟兄，察導訟者杖之，兄弟皆感悔。

translations.literal: when a younger brother sued an elder, he found who had instigated the suit and caned him; both brothers were moved to repentance.
translations.idiomatic: when a younger brother sued an elder, he found who had stirred up the suit, caned the agitator, and both brothers repented.

sentences.zh: 惡少以其徒為暴，校於衢，視其悔而釋之。

translations.literal: Ruffians led their gangs in violence; he flogged them in the street and released them when he saw repentance.
translations.idiomatic: When young hoodlums terrorized the streets with their gangs, he flogged them in public and released them once they showed remorse.

sentences.zh: 豪家僕奪負薪者妻，發吏捕治之，豪折節為善人。

translations.literal: A great family's servant seized a wood-cutter's wife; he sent officers to arrest and punish him, and the magnate restrained himself and became a good man.
translations.idiomatic: When a powerful family's servant seized a woodcutter's wife, he had the man arrested; the magnate then reformed and became a model citizen.

sentences.zh: 訟不以吏胥逮民，有宗族爭者以族長，有鄉里爭者以里老；

translations.literal: In lawsuits he did not use clerks and runners to seize the people; clan disputes went to clan elders, village disputes to village elders;
translations.idiomatic: He did not use runners to drag litigants to court: clan disputes went to clan elders, neighborhood quarrels to village elders;

sentences.zh: 又或使兩造相要俱至，謂之自追。

translations.literal: or he had both parties summon each other to come together, calling this "self-summons."
translations.idiomatic: or he had both parties summon each other to appear, a method he called "self-summons."

sentences.zh: 徵糧立掛比法，書其名以俟比，及數者自歸；

translations.literal: For tax collection he established the posted-assessment method, writing names to await assessment; when the amount was reached they came of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: For tax collection he posted names on a board; when a payer's quota was met he came forward on his own;

sentences.zh: 立甘限法，令以今限所不足倍輸於後。

translations.literal: he established the willing-deadline method, ordering that any shortfall in the current deadline be paid double in the next.
translations.idiomatic: and he allowed voluntary deadlines, with any shortfall paid double in the following period.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以軍興徵餉。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because of military campaigns, war funds were levied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1676 war levies were imposed for military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 隴其下令，謂「不戀一官，顧無益於爾民，而有害於急公」。

translations.literal: Longqi issued an order saying: "I do not cling to one office, but care that it bring no benefit to you people and harm urgent public service."
translations.idiomatic: Longqi proclaimed, "I do not cling to office for its own sake, but I will not squeeze the people for levies that do the public no good."

sentences.zh: 戶予一名刺勸諭之，不匝月，輸至十萬。

translations.literal: Each household was given a name slip for exhortation; within a month contributions reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Each household received a notice of appeal; within a month more than 100,000 taels were paid in.

sentences.zh: 會行間架稅，隴其謂當止於市肆，令毋及村舍。

translations.literal: When the building-frame tax was implemented, Longqi said it should stop at market shops and ordered that villages and dwellings not be touched.
translations.idiomatic: When a building-frame tax was introduced, he argued it should apply only to shops in town and ordered that farm villages be exempt.

sentences.zh: 江寧巡撫慕天顏請行州縣繁簡更調法，因言嘉定政繁多逋賦，隴其操守稱絕一塵，才幹乃非肆應，宜調簡縣。

translations.literal: Jiangning Governor Mu Tianyan requested implementation of the method for transferring officials between busy and easy counties, noting that Jiading had many administrative matters and tax arrears; Longqi's integrity was said to be without a speck of dust, yet his talent was not for versatile response—he should be transferred to an easy county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning Governor Mu Tianyan proposed rotating officials between busy and easy counties and reported that Jiading had heavy administration and tax arrears. Longqi's integrity was spotless, he said, but he lacked administrative flair and should be moved to a simpler county.

sentences.zh: 疏下部議，坐才力不及降調。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the ministries for deliberation; on the charge of insufficient ability he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the ministries, and he was demoted for inadequate ability.

sentences.zh: 縣民道為盜所殺而訟其仇，隴其獲盜定讞。

translations.literal: A county man named Dao was killed by bandits but sued his enemy; Longqi captured the bandits and fixed the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Dao was killed by bandits but had sued his personal enemy; Longqi caught the real bandits and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 部議初報不言盜，坐諱盜奪官。

translations.literal: The ministry's initial report did not mention bandits; on the charge of concealing banditry his office was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry's first report omitted mention of bandits, and he was dismissed for concealing banditry.

sentences.zh: 十七年，舉博學鴻儒，未及試，丁父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was nominated as an erudite scholar but before the examination entered mourning for his father and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1678 he was nominated for the erudite scholar examination but mourned his father's death before he could take it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，左都御史魏象樞應詔舉清廉官，疏薦隴其潔己愛民，去官日，惟圖書數卷及其妻織機一具，民愛之比於父母，命服闋以知縣用。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu, responding to an edict to recommend incorrupt officials, memorialized recommending Longqi for purifying himself and loving the people; on leaving office he had only a few scrolls of books and his wife's loom; the people loved him as they would parents; he was ordered that after mourning he be used again as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1679 Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu, answering an edict for recommendations of honest officials, praised Longqi's frugality and care for the people. When he left office he owned only a few books and his wife's loom, and the people loved him like parents. After mourning he was reappointed as a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授直隸靈壽知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed magistrate of Lingshou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1683 he was appointed magistrate of Lingshou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 靈壽土瘠民貧，役繁而俗薄。

translations.literal: Lingshou had poor soil and impoverished people, heavy corvée and shallow customs.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshou had poor soil, impoverished people, heavy corvée, and coarse habits.

sentences.zh: 隴其請於上官，與鄰縣更迭應役，俾得番代。

translations.literal: Longqi requested of his superiors that with neighboring counties corvée be taken in rotation so that turns could alternate.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his superiors to rotate corvée duties with neighboring counties so each could take turns.

sentences.zh: 行鄉約，察保甲，多為文告，反覆曉譬，務去鬥很輕生之習。

translations.literal: He implemented village compacts and inspected mutual-security groups, issuing many proclamations and repeatedly instructing, striving to remove the habits of brawling and treating life lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He revived village compacts and inspected mutual-security groups, issuing proclamations again and again to break the habits of brawling and reckless violence.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，直隸巡撫格爾古德以隴其與兗州知府張鵬翮同舉清廉官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Zhili Governor Ge'ergude recommended Longqi together with Yanzhou Prefect Zhang Penghe as incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1684 Zhili Governor Ge'ergude recommended Longqi along with Yanzhou Prefect Zhang Penghe as honest officials.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔九卿舉學問優長、品行可用者，隴其復被薦，得旨行取。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year an edict ordered the Nine Ministers to recommend those outstanding in learning and usable in conduct; Longqi was again recommended and received an edict for capital selection.
translations.idiomatic: In 1690 the Nine Ministers were ordered to recommend men of learning and good character; Longqi was nominated again and summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 隴其在靈壽七年，去官日，民遮道號泣，如去嘉定時。

translations.literal: Longqi was in Lingshou seven years; on the day he left office the people blocked the road weeping, as when he left Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in Lingshou, the people blocked his road weeping when he left, as they had at Jiading.

sentences.zh: 授四川道監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor of the Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a censor on the Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 偏沅巡撫於養誌有父喪，總督請在任守制。

translations.literal: Pian-Yuan Governor Yu Yangzhi had a father's death; the governor-general requested mourning in office.
translations.idiomatic: Pian-Yuan Governor Yu Yangzhi's father died, and the governor-general asked that he mourn in office.

sentences.zh: 隴其言天下承平，湖廣非用兵地，宜以孝教。

translations.literal: Longqi said the empire was at peace, Huguang was not a military region, and filial piety should be taught.
translations.idiomatic: Longqi argued that the empire was at peace, Huguang was not a war zone, and the court should teach filial duty by example.

sentences.zh: 養志解任。

translations.literal: Yangzhi was relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhi was ordered to leave office and mourn.

sentences.zh: 三十年，師徵噶爾丹，行捐納事例。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the army campaigned against Galdan and the purchase-of-office regulations were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1691, as troops marched against Galdan, the purchase-of-office regulations took effect.

sentences.zh: 御史陳菁請罷捐免保舉，而增捐應升先用，部議未行。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Jing requested abolishing purchase exemption from recommendation while increasing priority for purchased promotions; the ministries deliberated but did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Jing asked to end the sale of recommendation exemptions while giving purchased promotions priority; the ministries did not act.

sentences.zh: 隴其疏言：「捐納非上所欲行，若許捐免保舉，則與正途無異，且是清廉可捐納而得也；

translations.literal: Longqi memorialized: "Purchase of office is not what the emperor wishes to carry out; if purchase may exempt one from recommendation, then it is no different from the regular path, and integrity may be bought by payment;
translations.idiomatic: Longqi wrote, "Selling offices is not what Your Majesty wants. If men can buy exemption from recommendation, the purchased path becomes the same as the regular one, as though integrity could be bought;

sentences.zh: 至捐納先用，開奔競之途：皆不可行。

translations.literal: as for giving purchased men priority in promotion, that opens a path of frantic competition: none of these may be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: and giving purchased men priority in promotion opens the door to frantic competition. None of this should be allowed.

sentences.zh: 更請捐納之員三年無保舉，即予休致，以清仕途。

translations.literal: He further requested that purchased officials without recommendation within three years be granted retirement, to cleanse the official path.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that purchased officials who received no recommendation within three years be retired to keep the official path clean.

sentences.zh: 」九卿議，謂若行休致，則求保者奔競益甚。

translations.literal: " The Nine Ministers deliberated, saying that if retirement were implemented, those seeking recommendation would compete all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: " The Nine Ministers replied that forced retirement would only make men scramble harder for recommendations.

sentences.zh: 詔再與菁詳議，隴其又言：「捐納賢愚錯雜，惟恃保舉以防其弊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered further detailed deliberation with Jing; Longqi again said: "Purchased men mix the worthy with the foolish; only recommendation is relied on to guard against abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered further debate with Chen Jing. Longqi wrote again, "Purchased officials mix the capable with the worthless; only the recommendation system guards against abuse.

sentences.zh: 若並此而可捐納，此輩有不捐納者乎？

translations.literal: If even this may be purchased, would any of them not pay?
translations.idiomatic: If even that can be bought, who among them would not pay?

sentences.zh: 議者或謂三年無保舉即令休致為太刻，此輩白丁得官，踞民上者三年，亦已甚矣；

translations.literal: Some in deliberation said that requiring retirement after three years without recommendation was too harsh—these men obtained office from commoner status and sat above the people for three years, which is already excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Some objected that three years without recommendation followed by forced retirement was too harsh—commoners who bought office already ruled over the people for three years, which was harsh enough;

sentences.zh: 休致在家，儼然搢紳，為榮多矣。

translations.literal: retired at home, they would still be gentry in appearance—already much honor.
translations.idiomatic: and at home in retirement they would still rank as gentry, which was honor enough.

sentences.zh: 若云營求保舉，督撫而賢，何由奔競；

translations.literal: If one says that seeking recommendation leads to competition—if governors are worthy, whence comes frantic rivalry;
translations.idiomatic: As for the claim that men would scramble for recommendations—if governors and governors-general are worthy, why would there be frantic competition?

sentences.zh: 即不賢，亦不能盡人而保舉之也。

translations.literal: even if unworthy, they cannot recommend every person.
translations.idiomatic: And even if they were unworthy, they could not recommend everyone who paid.

sentences.zh: 」詞益激切。

translations.literal: His language grew ever more impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: His language grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 菁與九卿复持異議。

translations.literal: Jing and the Nine Ministers again held opposing views.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing and the Nine Ministers again disagreed.

sentences.zh: 戶部以捐生觀望，遲誤軍需，請奪隴其官，發奉天安置。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue, because purchased candidates were waiting and delaying military supplies, requested stripping Longqi of office and sending him to Fengtian for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue blamed him for slowing military funds because purchased candidates hesitated, and asked that he be dismissed and sent to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「隴其居官未久，不察事情，誠宜處分，但言官可貸。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Longqi has not been long in office and does not understand affairs—he truly should be punished, but as a remonstrating official he may be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Longqi has not been in office long and does not grasp the whole matter. He deserves punishment, but as a remonstrating official he may be spared.

sentences.zh: 」會順天府尹衛既齊巡畿輔，還奏民心皇皇，恐隴其遠謫，遂得免。

translations.literal: " It happened that Shuntian Prefect Wei Jiji was touring the capital region; returning he reported the people's hearts were anxious, fearing Longqi's distant banishment, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuntian Prefect Wei Jiji was touring the capital region and reported that the people were deeply alarmed at the prospect of Longqi's banishment. He was spared.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視北城。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect the North City.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon assigned to inspect the North City.

sentences.zh: 試俸滿，部議調外，因假歸。

translations.literal: When his probationary salary period ended, the ministries deliberated transferring him outside the capital, and he took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his probation ended, the ministries proposed transferring him outside the capital, and he went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1692.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，江南學政缺，上欲用隴其，侍臣奏隴其已卒，乃用邵嗣堯，嗣堯故與隴其同以清廉行取者也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the Jiangnan education commissionership was vacant; the emperor wished to use Longqi, but attendants reported Longqi had already died, so Shao Siyao was used—Siyao had formerly been selected to the capital together with Longqi for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1694 the Jiangnan education post fell vacant; the emperor wanted Longqi, but was told he had died, so Shao Siyao was appointed—another man who had entered the capital on a reputation for integrity like Longqi's.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，世宗臨雍，議增從祀諸儒，隴其與焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor attended the Imperial Academy and deliberated increasing attendant sacrifice for various Confucians; Longqi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1724 the Yongzheng Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and approved additional Confucians for attendant sacrifice, including Longqi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，特諡清獻，加贈內閣學士兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was specially posthumously titled Qingxian and additionally granted Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was given the posthumous title Qingxian and posthumously made Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 著有困勉錄、松陽講義、三魚堂文集。

translations.literal: He authored Records of Striving in Adversity, Lectures at Songyang, and the Collected Works of the Three-Fish Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Records of Striving in Adversity, Lectures at Songyang, and Collected Works of the Three-Fish Hall.

sentences.zh: 其為學專宗硃子，撰學術辨。

translations.literal: In learning he devoted himself solely to Zhu Xi and wrote Discriminations in Learning.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he followed Zhu Xi alone and wrote Discriminations in Learning.

sentences.zh: 大指謂王守仁以禪而託於儒，高攀龍、顧憲成知闢守仁，而以靜坐為主，本原之地不出守仁範圍，詆斥之甚力。

translations.literal: Its main import was that Wang Shouren cloaked Chan in Confucian garb; Gao Panlong and Gu Xiancheng knew how to refute Shouren yet took quiet-sitting as primary—their ground of origin still did not escape Shouren's scope—and he denounced them with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Its main argument was that Wang Yangming dressed Chan Buddhism in Confucian robes; Gao Panlong and Gu Xiancheng saw through Wang yet still made quiet-sitting central and never escaped his framework, and Longqi denounced them sharply.

sentences.zh: 為縣崇實政，嘉定民頌隴其，迄清季未已。

translations.literal: As magistrate he honored practical administration; Jiading people praised Longqi, and this continued to the end of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: As a magistrate he prized practical governance, and the people of Jiading praised him into the late Qing.

sentences.zh: 靈壽鄰縣阜平為置塚，民陸氏世守焉，自號隴其子孫。

translations.literal: In neighboring Fuping of Lingshou a tomb was set up for him; the commoner Lu clan guarded it for generations and called themselves Longqi's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring Fuping county built him a tomb, which the Lu family guarded for generations, calling themselves Longqi's descendants.

sentences.zh: 張伯行，字孝先，河南儀封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Boxing, style name Xiaoxian, was a native of Yifeng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boxing, whose style was Xiaoxian, came from Yifeng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年進士，考授內閣中書，改中書科中書。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi, was examined and appointed Secretariat secretary, and was transferred to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1685, entered the Grand Secretariat as a secretary, and became a drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂歸，建請見書院，講明正學。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father and returned home, building the Qingjian Academy to expound orthodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he returned home and founded the Qingjian Academy to teach orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 儀封城北舊有堤，三十八年六月，大雨，潰，伯行募民囊土塞之。

translations.literal: North of Yifeng city there was an old dike; in the sixth month of the thirty-eighth year great rain breached it, and Boxing recruited the people to bag earth and block it.
translations.idiomatic: An old dike north of Yifeng burst in the sixth month of 1699 after heavy rains; Boxing rallied the people to fill the breach with earth in sacks.

sentences.zh: 河道總督張鵬翮行河，疏薦堪理河務，命以原銜赴河工，督修黃河南岸堤二百餘裡及馬家港、東壩、高家堰諸工。

translations.literal: River Conservancy Director Zhang Penghe was inspecting the rivers and memorialized recommending him as capable of managing river works; he was ordered with his original rank to go to river projects, supervising repair of more than two hundred li of dike on the Yellow River's south bank and works at Majiagang, Dongba, and Gaojiayan.
translations.idiomatic: River Director Zhang Penghe, touring the waterways, recommended him for river work. Retaining his rank, Boxing was sent to supervise more than two hundred li of dikes on the south bank of the Yellow River and projects at Majiagang, Dongba, and Gaojiayan.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，授山東濟寧道。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was appointed Jining Circuit commissioner in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1703 he was appointed commissioner of the Jining Circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 值歲饑，即家運錢米，並製棉衣，拯民飢寒。

translations.literal: When famine struck that year, he immediately transported money and grain from home and also made cotton coats to save the people from hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, he shipped money and grain from his own household and had cotton coats made to relieve hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 上命分道治賑，伯行賑汶上、陽穀二縣，發倉穀二萬二千六百石有奇。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered relief by separate circuits; Boxing relieved Wenshang and Yanggu counties, issuing more than twenty-two thousand six hundred shi of grain from the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered circuit-by-circuit relief; Boxing aided Wenshang and Yanggu, releasing more than 22,600 shi of grain from the granaries.

sentences.zh: 布政使責其專擅，即論劾，伯行曰：「有旨治賑，不得為專擅。

translations.literal: The provincial treasurer blamed him for acting on his own authority and immediately memorialized impeachment; Boxing said: "There was an edict to administer relief—this cannot be called usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial treasurer accused him of acting without authorization and impeached him. Boxing replied, "There was an edict to relieve famine. That is not usurpation.

sentences.zh: 上視民如傷，倉穀重乎？

translations.literal: The emperor regards the people as wounded—are granary stores heavier?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treats the people as wounded bodies. Are granary stores heavier

sentences.zh: 人命重乎？

translations.literal: Are human lives heavier?"
translations.idiomatic: than human lives?"

sentences.zh: 」乃得寢。

translations.literal: Only then was the matter shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The impeachment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，上南巡，賜「布澤安流」榜。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, on the emperor's southern tour, he was granted a plaque reading "Spreading Blessings, Settling the Current."
translations.idiomatic: In 1706, on the emperor's southern tour, he received a plaque inscribed "Spreading Blessings, Settling the Current."

sentences.zh: 尋遷江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Jiangsu Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Jiangsu surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，复南巡，至蘇州，諭從臣曰：「朕聞張伯行居官甚清，最不易得。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, on another southern tour, reaching Suzhou, he told his attendants: "I have heard Zhang Boxing in office is very pure—the most difficult to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1707, on another southern tour, the emperor reached Suzhou and told his attendants, "I have heard Zhang Boxing is exceptionally clean in office—the rarest of qualities.

sentences.zh: 」時命所在督撫舉賢能官，伯行不與。

translations.literal: " At the time an order went out for governors and governors-general to recommend worthy officials; Boxing did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: " Governors were then ordered to recommend able officials, but Boxing did not nominate anyone.

sentences.zh: 上見伯行曰：「朕久識汝，朕自舉之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Boxing and said: "I have long known you; I myself will recommend you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I have known you a long time. I will recommend you myself.

sentences.zh: 他日居官而善，天下以朕為知人。

translations.literal: If in future in office you do well, the empire will take me as one who knows men."
translations.idiomatic: If you serve well hereafter, the world will say I know how to choose men."

sentences.zh: 」擢福建巡撫，賜「廉惠宣猷」榜。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Fujian governor and granted a plaque reading "Integrity, Kindness, and Spreading Merit."
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Fujian and given a plaque reading "Integrity, Kindness, and Spreading Merit."

sentences.zh: 伯行疏請免台灣、鳳山、諸羅三縣荒賦。

translations.literal: Boxing memorialized requesting remission of wasteland taxes in the three counties of Taiwan, Fengshan, and Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing asked remission of wasteland taxes for Taiwan, Fengshan, and Zhuluo.

sentences.zh: 福建米貴，請發帑五萬巿湖廣、江西、廣東米平糶。

translations.literal: Grain was dear in Fujian; he requested fifty thousand taels from the treasury to buy rice in Huguang, Jiangxi, and Guangdong and sell it at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: When grain prices rose in Fujian, he asked for fifty thousand taels to buy rice in Huguang, Jiangxi, and Guangdong and sell it at fair rates.

sentences.zh: 建鼇峰書院，置學舍，出所藏書，搜先儒文集刊佈為正誼堂叢書，以教諸生。

translations.literal: He built Aofeng Academy, set up dormitories, brought out his collected books, searched out collected works of earlier Confucians and published them as the Zhengyi Hall Series to instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Aofeng Academy, built dormitories, lent out his library, and published collected works of earlier Confucians as the Zhengyi Hall Series for his students.

sentences.zh: 福州民祀瘟神，命毀其偶像，改祠為義塾，祀硃子。

translations.literal: Fuzhou people worshipped the plague god; he ordered its idols destroyed, the shrine converted to a charity school, and Zhu Xi worshipped there.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhou people worshipped a plague god, he destroyed the idols, turned the shrine into a charity school, and installed Zhu Xi in worship.

sentences.zh: 俗多尼，鬻貧家女，髡之至千百，伯行命其家贖還擇偶，貧不能贖，官為出之。

translations.literal: The custom had many nuns who sold poor families' daughters and tonsured them by the hundreds and thousands; Boxing ordered families to ransom them back and choose husbands; those too poor to ransom, the government paid out.
translations.idiomatic: Nuns commonly bought poor girls and tonsured them by the hundreds; Boxing ordered families to ransom their daughters and marry them off, paying from public funds when families could not.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，調江蘇巡撫，賑淮、揚、徐三府飢。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was transferred to Jiangsu governor and relieved famine in Huai, Yang, and Xu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 1709 he became Jiangsu governor and relieved famine in Huai, Yang, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 會布政使宜思恭以司庫虧空為總督噶禮劾罷，上遣尚書張鵬翮按治。

translations.literal: It happened that Provincial Treasurer Yi Sigong was impeached and dismissed by Governor-General Gali for treasury deficits; the emperor sent Minister Zhang Penghe to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Treasurer Yi Sigong was impeached and dismissed by Governor-General Gali for treasury shortfalls, and the emperor sent Minister Zhang Penghe to investigate.

sentences.zh: 陳鵬年以蘇州知府署布政使，議司庫虧三十四萬，分扣官俸役食抵補，伯行諮噶禮會題，不應。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian as Suzhou prefect acted as provincial treasurer and proposed that the treasury deficit of three hundred forty thousand be covered by deducting officials' salaries and runners' rations; Boxing consulted Gali for joint memorial, but he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian, acting treasurer as Suzhou prefect, proposed covering a 340,000-tael deficit by docking salaries and ration payments. Boxing asked Gali to co-sign the memorial; Gali refused.

sentences.zh: 伯行疏上聞，上命鵬翮並按。

translations.literal: Boxing memorialized to inform the throne; the emperor ordered Penghe to investigate together.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing reported directly to the throne, and the emperor ordered Penghe to investigate as well.

sentences.zh: 別疏陳噶禮異議狀，上諭廷臣曰：「覽伯行此疏，知與噶禮不和。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he stated Gali's dissent; the emperor instructed court officials: "Reading this memorial of Boxing, I know he and Gali are not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he described Gali's opposition. The emperor told the court, "This memorial shows Boxing and Gali are at odds.

sentences.zh: 為人臣者，當以國事為重。

translations.literal: As subjects, you should take state affairs as paramount.
translations.idiomatic: As ministers you must put state affairs first.

sentences.zh: 朕綜理機務垂五十年，未嘗令一人得逞其私。

translations.literal: I have managed state affairs for nearly fifty years and never let one person achieve his private ends.
translations.idiomatic: I have governed for nearly fifty years and never let anyone serve private ends at court.

sentences.zh: 此疏宜置不問。

translations.literal: This memorial should be set aside without inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: Set this memorial aside."

sentences.zh: 」伯行尋乞病，上不許。

translations.literal: Boxing soon pleaded illness; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing soon asked to retire on grounds of illness, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮請責前任巡撫於準及思恭償十六萬，餘以官俸役食抵補。

translations.literal: Penghe requested that former governors Yu Zhun and Sigong repay one hundred sixty thousand, the remainder covered by salaries and rations.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe proposed that former governors Yu Zhun and Sigong repay 160,000 taels and that the rest be covered by salary deductions.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「江南虧空錢糧，非官吏侵蝕。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jiangnan's deficits in grain and silver were not from officials' embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jiangnan's tax shortfalls were not caused by embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 朕南巡時，督撫肆意挪用而不敢言。

translations.literal: On my southern tours, governors and governors-general diverted funds at will and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: On my southern tours, governors diverted funds freely and dared not report it.

sentences.zh: 若責新任官補償，朕心實有不忍。

translations.literal: If new appointees are charged to make compensation, my heart truly cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to make new appointees pay for it.

sentences.zh: 」命察明南巡時用款具奏。

translations.literal: He ordered investigation of expenditures during the southern tours to be memorialized in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full accounting of southern-tour expenditures.

sentences.zh: 伯行又疏奏各府州縣無著錢糧十萬八千，上命並予豁免。

translations.literal: Boxing again memorialized that unaccounted grain and silver in all prefectures and counties totaled one hundred eight thousand; the emperor ordered all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing also reported 108,000 taels in unallocated taxes across the province, and the emperor ordered them all remitted.

sentences.zh: 噶禮貪橫，伯行與之迕。

translations.literal: Gali was greedy and overbearing; Boxing clashed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gali was greedy and domineering, and Boxing stood against him.

sentences.zh: 五十年，江南鄉試副考官趙晉交通關節，榜發，士論譁然，輿財神入學宮。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, Jiangnan provincial examination associate examiner Zhao Jin trafficked in influence; when the list was published, scholarly opinion was in uproar, and they carried the God of Wealth into the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1711 the associate examiner Zhao Jin was caught taking bribes in the Jiangnan provincial exams. When the results were posted, scholars were outraged and paraded the God of Wealth into the examination hall.

sentences.zh: 伯行疏上其事，正考官左必蕃亦以實聞，命尚書張鵬翮、侍郎赫壽按治，伯行與噶禮會鞫，得舉人吳泌、程光奎通賄狀，詞連噶禮。

translations.literal: Boxing memorialized reporting the matter; chief examiner Zuo Bifan also reported the facts; Ministers Zhang Penghe and Vice Minister Hesou were ordered to investigate; Boxing and Gali jointly examined and obtained evidence that juren Wu Mi and Cheng Guangkui had trafficked in bribes, testimony implicating Gali.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing reported the scandal; chief examiner Zuo Bifan confirmed it. Ministers Zhang Penghe and Hesou were sent to investigate. At a joint hearing with Gali, evidence showed that degree holders Wu Mi and Cheng Guangkui had taken bribes, with testimony implicating Gali.

sentences.zh: 伯行請解噶禮任付嚴審，噶禮不自安，亦摭伯行七罪訐奏。

translations.literal: Boxing requested relieving Gali of duty for strict trial; Gali, ill at ease, also gathered seven charges against Boxing and memorialized in accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing asked that Gali be removed and tried strictly. Uneasy, Gali countered with seven charges against Boxing.

sentences.zh: 上命俱解任，鵬翮等尋奏晉與泌、光奎通賄俱實，擬罪如律；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered both relieved of duty; Penghe and others soon memorialized that Jin's bribery with Mi and Guangkui was all true and proposed punishment according to law;
translations.idiomatic: Both were suspended. Penghe reported that Zhao Jin, Wu Mi, and Cheng Guangkui had indeed taken bribes and proposed legal punishment;

sentences.zh: 噶禮交通事誣，伯行應奪官。

translations.literal: Gali's trafficking was false, and Boxing should be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: but declared Gali's involvement false and said Boxing should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上切責鵬翮等掩飾，更命尚書穆和倫、張廷樞覆按，仍如前議。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked Penghe and others for concealment and ordered Ministers Mu Helun and Zhang Tingshu to reinvestigate; they still deliberated as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked them for covering up the facts and sent Ministers Mu Helun and Zhang Tingshu to reinvestigate, but they returned the same verdict.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「伯行居官清正，天下所知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Boxing in office is pure and upright, as all the empire knows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Everyone knows Boxing is upright in office.

sentences.zh: 噶禮才雖有餘而喜生事，無清正名。

translations.literal: Gali's talent, though more than sufficient, delights in stirring trouble and has no name for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Gali is capable but loves trouble and has no reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 此議是非顛倒，命九卿、詹事、科道再議。

translations.literal: This deliberation inverts right and wrong; order the Nine Ministers, Household tutors, and censorate to deliberate again."
translations.idiomatic: This verdict turns truth upside down. The Nine Ministers, tutors, and censors must deliberate again."

sentences.zh: 」明日，召九卿等諭曰：「伯行居官清廉，噶禮操守朕不能信。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned the Nine Ministers and instructed: "Boxing in office is clean; Gali's conduct I cannot trust.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the Nine Ministers, "Boxing is clean in office. I do not trust Gali's conduct.

sentences.zh: 若無伯行，則江南必受其朘削幾半矣。

translations.literal: Without Boxing, Jiangnan would surely suffer his draining of nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Without Boxing, Jiangnan would have been drained of nearly half its wealth by Gali.

sentences.zh: 此互參一案，初遣官往審，為噶禮所製，致不能得其情；

translations.literal: In this mutual impeachment case, the first officials sent to investigate were manipulated by Gali, so the truth could not be obtained;
translations.idiomatic: In this mutual impeachment, the first investigators were controlled by Gali and could not learn the truth;

sentences.zh: 再遣官往審，與前無異。

translations.literal: the second officials sent to investigate were no different from before.
translations.idiomatic: the second team was no better.

sentences.zh: 爾等能體朕保全清官之意，使正人無所疑懼，則海宇昇平矣。

translations.literal: If you can embody my intent to preserve clean officials and let upright men be without doubt or fear, then the realm will be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: If you grasp my wish to protect honest officials so upright men need not fear, the realm will be at peace.

sentences.zh: 」遂奪噶禮官，命伯行復任。

translations.literal: Gali's office was then taken and Boxing ordered to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gali was dismissed and Boxing restored.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，江蘇布政使缺員，伯行疏薦福建布政使李發甲、台灣道陳瑸、前祭酒余正健，上已以湖北按察使牟欽元擢任。
