translations.literal: In the fifty-second year the Jiangsu provincial treasurer post was vacant; Boxing memorialized recommending Fujian Provincial Treasurer Li Fajia, Taiwan Circuit Intendant Chen Bin, and former Libationer Yu Zhengjian; the emperor had already promoted Hubei Surveillance Commissioner Mou Qinyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1713 the Jiangsu provincial treasurer post fell vacant. Boxing recommended Li Fajia, Chen Bin, and Yu Zhengjian, but the emperor had already appointed Mou Qinyuan from Hubei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，伯行劾欽元匿通海罪人張令濤署中，請逮治。

translations.literal: Before long Boxing impeached Qinyuan for harboring Zhang Lingtao, a man connected with maritime crime, in his yamen, and requested arrest and trial.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Boxing impeached Qinyuan for hiding Zhang Lingtao, a man implicated in maritime crime, in his offices and asked that he be arrested.

sentences.zh: 令濤兄元隆居上海，造海船，出入海洋，擁厚貲，結納豪貴。

translations.literal: Lingtao's elder brother Yuanlong lived in Shanghai, built seagoing vessels, went in and out of the ocean, possessed great wealth, and cultivated connections with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Lingtao's brother Yuanlong lived in Shanghai, built seagoing ships, traded on the ocean, amassed great wealth, and cultivated ties with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 會部檄搜緝海賊鄭盡心餘黨，崇明水師捕漁船，其舟人福建產，冒華亭籍，驗船照為元隆所代領，伯行欲窮治。

translations.literal: It happened that the ministry ordered search for remnants of pirate Zheng Jin's faction; Chongming naval forces seized a fishing boat whose sailors were Fujian natives posing as Huating registrants; verifying the boat license showed Yuanlong had taken it on their behalf; Boxing wished to pursue the case to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry ordered a hunt for remnants of the pirate Zheng Jin's gang, Chongming naval forces seized a fishing boat whose crew were Fujian men posing as Huating natives. The license proved Yuanlong had obtained it for them, and Boxing sought a full prosecution.

sentences.zh: 是時令濤在噶禮幕，元隆稱病不就逮，獄未竟而死於家。

translations.literal: At the time Lingtao was in Gali's staff; Yuanlong claimed illness and did not submit to arrest; before the case ended he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Lingtao was then on Gali's staff. Yuanlong pleaded illness and evaded arrest, then died at home before trial ended.

sentences.zh: 噶禮前劾伯行，因摭其事為七罪之一。

translations.literal: When Gali had earlier impeached Boxing, he made this affair one of the seven charges.
translations.idiomatic: Gali had made this case one of his seven charges against Boxing.

sentences.zh: 會上海縣民顧協一訴令濤據其房屋，別有水寨數處窩藏海賊，稱令濤今居欽元署中。

translations.literal: It happened that Shanghai county man Gu Xieyi sued that Lingtao had seized his house and that elsewhere several water stockades harbored pirates; he said Lingtao now resided in Qinyuan's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Then a Shanghai county man named Gu Xieyi sued Lingtao for seizing his house and said several river strongholds harbored pirates; he reported Lingtao was living in Qinyuan's offices.

sentences.zh: 上命總督赫壽察審，赫壽庇令濤，以通賊無證聞；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Governor Hesou to investigate; Hesou shielded Lingtao and reported no evidence of trafficking with pirates;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Governor Hesou to investigate. Hesou protected Lingtao and reported no evidence of collusion with pirates;

sentences.zh: 復命鵬翮及副都御史阿錫鼐按其事，鵬翮等奏元隆、令濤皆良民，請奪伯行官。

translations.literal: he again ordered Penghe and Vice Censor-in-Chief A Xitai to investigate; Penghe and others memorialized that Yuanlong and Lingtao were all good subjects and requested stripping Boxing of office.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe and Vice Censor-in-Chief A Xitai were sent next. They reported Yuanlong and Lingtao were honest men and asked that Boxing be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上命復審，且命伯行自陳，伯行疏言：「元隆通賊，雖報身故，而金多黨眾，人人可以冒名，處處可以領照。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered reinvestigation and also ordered Boxing to state his own case; Boxing memorialized: "Yuanlong trafficked with pirates; though reported dead, with much gold and many followers, anyone can assume a false name and obtain licenses everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a new inquiry and asked Boxing to defend himself. Boxing wrote, "Yuanlong colluded with pirates. Though reported dead, his wealth and network mean anyone can use his name and obtain licenses anywhere.

sentences.zh: 令濤乃顧協一首告，若其不實，例應坐誣；

translations.literal: Lingtao was first accused by Gu Xieyi; if untrue, by statute he should be charged with false accusation;
translations.idiomatic: Lingtao was first accused by Gu Xieyi. If the charge is false, Gu should be punished for false accusation;

sentences.zh: 欽元庇匿，致案久懸。

translations.literal: Qinyuan shielded and concealed him, causing the case to hang long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Qinyuan shielded him and let the case drag on.

sentences.zh: 臣為地方大吏，杜漸防微，豈得不究？

translations.literal: I as a great local official, stopping evil at its first sprout—how can I not pursue it?"
translations.idiomatic: As a senior local official charged with stopping trouble early, how could I not pursue it?"

sentences.zh: 」既命解任，鵬翮等仍以伯行誣陷良民、挾詐欺公，論斬，法司議如所擬，上免其罪，命伯行來京。

translations.literal: After he was ordered relieved, Penghe and others still charged Boxing with framing good subjects and using fraud to deceive the public, proposing decapitation; the judiciary deliberated as proposed; the emperor pardoned his offense and ordered Boxing to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though dismissed, Penghe still charged him with framing innocent men and deceiving the public, proposing execution. The judiciary agreed, but the emperor spared him and summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 旋入直南書房，署倉場侍郎，充順天鄉試正考官。

translations.literal: Soon he entered service in the Southern Study, acted as granary vice minister, and served as chief examiner of the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the Southern Study, served as acting granary vice minister, and was chief examiner for the Shuntian provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 授戶部侍郎，兼管錢法、倉場，再充會試副考官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, also managing coinage law and granaries, and again served as associate metropolitan examination examiner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Revenue, oversaw coinage and granaries, and served again as associate metropolitan examination examiner.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢禮部尚書，賜「禮樂名臣」榜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to Minister of Rites and granted a plaque reading "Famed Minister of Ritual and Music."
translations.idiomatic: In 1723 he was made Minister of Rites and given a plaque reading "Famed Minister of Ritual and Music."

sentences.zh: 二年，命赴闕里祭崇聖祠。

translations.literal: In the second year he was ordered to go to Qufu to sacrifice at the Shrine of the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: In 1724 he was sent to Qufu to sacrifice at the Sage's shrine.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1725 at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 遺疏請崇正學，勵直臣。

translations.literal: His final memorial requested honoring orthodox learning and encouraging upright ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial asked the court to honor orthodox learning and encourage upright ministers.

sentences.zh: 上軫悼，贈太子太保，諡清恪。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Qingke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Qingke.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，從祀文廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was granted attendant sacrifice in the literary temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu era he was admitted to attendant sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 伯行方成進士，歸構精舍於南郊，陳書數千卷縱觀之，及小學、近思錄，程、硃語類，曰：「入聖門庭在是矣。

translations.literal: When Boxing had just become a jinshi, he returned and built a refined studio in the southern suburbs, spread out several thousand scrolls to read at will, and reaching the Elementary Learning, Reflections on Things at Hand, and classified sayings of Cheng and Zhu, said: "The gateway to sagehood lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from the jinshi examination, Boxing built a study in the southern suburbs, spread out thousands of books, and upon reaching the Elementary Learning, Reflections on Things at Hand, and the classified sayings of Cheng and Zhu, declared, "The gate to sagehood is here.

sentences.zh: 」盡發濂、洛、關、閩諸大儒之書，口誦手抄者七年。

translations.literal: " He brought forth all the books of the great Confucians of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min schools and for seven years recited aloud and copied by hand.
translations.idiomatic: " He then studied the works of the Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min masters, reciting and copying them for seven years.

sentences.zh: 始赴官，嘗曰：「千聖之學，括於一敬，故學莫先於主敬。

translations.literal: When he first took office he once said: "The learning of a thousand sages is summed up in reverence; therefore in learning nothing comes before holding reverence.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he said, "The learning of a thousand sages is summed up in reverence. Nothing in study comes before cultivating reverence.

sentences.zh: 」因自號曰敬庵。

translations.literal: " He therefore styled himself the Hermitage of Reverence.
translations.idiomatic: " He took the style Hermitage of Reverence.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「君子喻於義，小人喻於利。

translations.literal: He also said: "The noble man is instructed by righteousness, the petty man by profit.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The noble man understands duty; the petty man understands profit.

sentences.zh: 老氏貪生，佛者畏死，烈士徇名，皆利也。

translations.literal: The Daoist covets life, the Buddhist fears death, the martyr dies for a name—all are profit."
translations.idiomatic: Daoists cling to life, Buddhists fear death, martyrs die for fame—all are forms of profit."

sentences.zh: 」在官所引，皆學問醇正，志操潔清，初不令知。

translations.literal: Those he brought into office were all sound in learning and pure in conduct, without letting them know beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Those he appointed were men of sound learning and pure conduct, chosen without their knowing in advance.

sentences.zh: 平日齮齕之者，復與共事，推誠協恭，無絲毫芥蒂。

translations.literal: Those who had gnashed at him in daily life he again worked with, extending sincerity and mutual respect, without the slightest grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had once resented him he worked with again in sincerity, without a trace of bitterness.

sentences.zh: 曰：「已荷保全，敢以私廢公乎？

translations.literal: He said: "Having already received preservation, how dare I let private feeling waste public duty?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The throne has protected me. How could I let private grievance interfere with public duty?"

sentences.zh: 」所著有困學錄、續錄、正誼堂文集、居濟一得諸書。

translations.literal: His works include Records of Hard Learning, Continued Records, Collected Works of the Zhengyi Hall, and One Gain in Dwelling in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Records of Hard Learning, Continued Records, Collected Works of the Zhengyi Hall, and One Gain in Dwelling in Ji.

sentences.zh: 子師載，字又渠。

translations.literal: His son Shizai, style name Youqu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizai, styled Youqu,

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: was a provincial graduate

sentences.zh: 以父廕補戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: and entered the Ministry of Revenue as a vice director through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，授揚州知府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was appointed Yangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he became prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，高郵湖西民以縣吏報災輕，不得賑。

translations.literal: In a famine year, people west of Gaoyou Lake, because county clerks reported the disaster lightly, could not obtain relief.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine, people west of Gaoyou Lake could not get relief because county clerks had underreported the disaster.

sentences.zh: 師載行部，見饑民滿道，不待報而賑之。

translations.literal: Shizai was on circuit and, seeing famine victims filling the roads, relieved them without awaiting approval.
translations.idiomatic: On circuit Shizai saw starving people filling the roads and distributed relief without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 江都芒稻閘為淮、黃，高、寶諸河入江要津，夏潦盛漲。

translations.literal: The Mangdao sluice in Jiangdu was the critical junction where the Huai, Yellow, and Gaoyou and Baoying rivers entered the Yangzi; in summer floods swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Mangdao sluice in Jiangdu was the key junction where the Huai, Yellow, and Gaoyou rivers entered the Yangzi, and summer floods ran high.

sentences.zh: 閘官利商人餌，謂非運使令不得啟。

translations.literal: Sluice officials profited from merchants' bribes and said the sluice could not be opened without the transport intendant's order.
translations.idiomatic: Sluice officials took merchants' bribes and refused to open the gates without the salt intendant's order.

sentences.zh: 師載詢鹽艘須水六七尺，今過半，乃身往督役啟閘。

translations.literal: Shizai inquired that salt boats needed six or seven chi of water; now more than half that depth was present, so he went in person to supervise workers in opening the sluice.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that salt barges needed six or seven chi of water and that more than half that depth was present, he went in person to have the sluice opened.

sentences.zh: 其後芒稻閘屬府啟閉，遂以為例。

translations.literal: Thereafter opening and closing the Mangdao sluice fell under the prefecture, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the prefecture controlled the Mangdao sluice, and that became precedent.

sentences.zh: 累遷江蘇按察使，內擢右通政。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Jiangsu surveillance commissioner and elevated within the capital to right vice commissioner of communications.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiangsu surveillance commissioner and then to right vice commissioner of communications in the capital.

sentences.zh: 再遷，授倉場侍郎，命協辦江南河務。

translations.literal: Promoted again, he was appointed granary vice minister and ordered to assist in Jiangnan river works.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again, he became granary vice minister and was assigned to assist Jiangnan river works.

sentences.zh: 授安徽巡撫，仍命赴南河協同防護。

translations.literal: He was appointed Anhui governor and still ordered to go to the Southern Rivers to assist in protection jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Anhui but still ordered to the Southern Rivers to help with flood defense.

sentences.zh: 會河溢，奪官。

translations.literal: When the river overflowed, his office was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the river burst its banks, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上命誅疏防同知李焞、守備張賓，使師載視行刑，畢，釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered execution of Assistant Prefect Li Kun and Garrison Commander Zhang Bin for negligence in flood defense, had Shizai witness the execution, and after it was done released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the execution of Assistant Prefect Li Kun and Garrison Commander Zhang Bin for flood negligence and made Shizai witness it before restoring him to office.

sentences.zh: 再起為兵部侍郎，遷漕運總督。

translations.literal: He was restored as Vice Minister of War and transferred to Grain Transport Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Vice Minister of War and made Grain Transport Director.

sentences.zh: 复授河東河道總督。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Eastern River Conservancy in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed director of the Eastern River Conservancy.

sentences.zh: 師載長於治河。

translations.literal: Shizai excelled at river management.
translations.idiomatic: Shizai excelled at river management.

sentences.zh: 少讀父書，研性理之學，高宗稱其篤實。

translations.literal: In youth he read his father's books and studied moral philosophy; the Gaozong Emperor called him solid and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied his father's books and moral philosophy from youth, and the Qianlong Emperor called him solid and sincere.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，諡愨敬。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Quejing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Quejing.

sentences.zh: 論曰：清世以名臣從祀孔子廟，斌、隴其、伯行三人而已，皆以外吏起家，蒙聖祖恩遇。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Qing, only Bin, Longqi, and Boxing among famed ministers were granted attendant sacrifice in the Confucian temple—all rose from outer-service posts and received the favor of the Sage Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In the Qing, only Bin, Longqi, and Boxing among renowned ministers were admitted to attendant sacrifice in the Confucian temple. All rose from provincial service and enjoyed the Kangxi Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 隴其官止御史，而廉能清正，民愛之如父母，與斌、伯行如一，其不為時所容而為聖祖所愛護也亦如一。

translations.literal: Longqi's office reached only censor, yet he was incorrupt, capable, and pure; the people loved him as parents—like Bin and Boxing—and his not being tolerated by the age yet being protected by the Sage Ancestor was likewise the same.
translations.idiomatic: Longqi rose only to censor, yet the people loved him like parents, as they did Bin and Boxing. He too was ill tolerated by his peers yet protected by the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 君明而臣良，漢、唐以後，蓋亦罕矣。

translations.literal: A clear-sighted ruler and good ministers—since Han and Tang, this has been rare indeed.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler and worthy ministers—since Han and Tang, such a pairing has been rare.

sentences.zh: 斌不薄王守仁，隴其篤守程、硃，斥守仁甚峻，而伯行繼之。

translations.literal: Bin did not slight Wang Shouren; Longqi devotedly upheld Cheng and Zhu and denounced Shouren very sternly, and Boxing followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin did not dismiss Wang Yangming; Longqi held firmly to Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi and denounced Wang sharply; Boxing followed Longqi in that regard.

sentences.zh: 要其躬行實踐，施於政事，皆能無負其所學，雖趨鄉稍有廣隘，亦無所軒輊焉。

translations.literal: What matters is that in personal practice applied to government affairs, all could live up to their learning; though their schools of thought differed slightly in breadth and narrowness, there is nothing to rank one above another.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is that all three lived their principles in government and did not betray their learning. Though their schools of thought differed in breadth, none should be ranked above the others.
